## 1. Which published systems track progress explicitly and replan on stalls, and how exactly?

### Takeaway
Two families exist. LLM-judged progress ledgers (Magentic-One) ask the model every round whether it is looping or progressing and replan with a full context reset after about 3 stalled rounds. Deterministic guards (OpenHands, Gemini CLI, Browser Use) hash actions and observations and fire at 3 to 5 exact repeats, but all three mostly respond with a text nudge or a halt, not a block. No shipping system I read refuses the repeated action and forces an alternative.

### Cited Findings

**Magentic-One / AutoGen (2024, maintained through 2026)**
- The orchestrator runs two loops. The outer loop builds a task ledger: a fact sheet with four headings (given or verified facts, facts to look up, facts to derive, educated guesses) and a short bullet plan. The inner loop fills a progress ledger every round. — [autogen `_prompts.py`](https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/blob/main/python/packages/autogen-agentchat/src/autogen_agentchat/teams/_group_chat/_magentic_one/_prompts.py)
- The progress ledger is one JSON object with five keys, each holding a `reason` and an `answer`: `is_request_satisfied` (bool), `is_in_loop` (bool), `is_progress_being_made` (bool), `next_speaker` (name), `instruction_or_question` (text). Paraphrase of the loop question: are we repeating the same requests or getting the same responses as before; loops may span several turns and include repeated actions such as scrolling more than a handful of times. Paraphrase of the progress question: true if just starting or recent messages add value; false if recent messages show a loop or a significant barrier such as being unable to read a required file. — [autogen `_prompts.py`](https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/blob/main/python/packages/autogen-agentchat/src/autogen_agentchat/teams/_group_chat/_magentic_one/_prompts.py)
- Stall counter logic, exact: if `is_progress_being_made` is false, `n_stalls += 1`; else if `is_in_loop` is true, `n_stalls += 1`; otherwise `n_stalls = max(0, n_stalls - 1)`. When `n_stalls >= max_stalls` the orchestrator updates the task ledger and re-enters the outer loop. Progress therefore decays the counter by one; it does not zero it. — [autogen `_magentic_one_orchestrator.py`](https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/blob/main/python/packages/autogen-agentchat/src/autogen_agentchat/teams/_group_chat/_magentic_one/_magentic_one_orchestrator.py)
- The paper states the counter is kept at or below 2 in the experiments and replanning happens when it exceeds 2, which matches a `max_stalls` of 3. — [Magentic-One paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.04468)
- Replanning is two model calls. First the fact sheet is rewritten; paraphrase: it is clear we are not progressing as hoped, rewrite the fact sheet with anything learned, move guesses to verified facts where justified, and add or update at least one educated guess with reasoning. Then the plan is rewritten; paraphrase: briefly explain what went wrong on the last run (the root cause), then give a new concise bullet plan with hints that overcome the earlier obstacles and avoid repeating the same mistakes. — [autogen `_prompts.py`](https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/blob/main/python/packages/autogen-agentchat/src/autogen_agentchat/teams/_group_chat/_magentic_one/_prompts.py)
- On re-entering the outer loop the orchestrator sends a reset message to every participant, clears its own message thread, and re-broadcasts only the new ledger (task, team, facts, plan). Every agent restarts with a clean context. — [autogen `_magentic_one_orchestrator.py`](https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/blob/main/python/packages/autogen-agentchat/src/autogen_agentchat/teams/_group_chat/_magentic_one/_magentic_one_orchestrator.py)
- Measured effect: replacing the ledger orchestrator with a simple group-chat orchestrator drops GAIA validation performance by 31% (GPT-4o). Removing a single agent drops it by 21% to 39%. — [Magentic-One paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.04468)
- Error analysis: the most common error code is persistent-inefficient-actions (agents continue unproductive patterns without adapting after failures), the second is insufficient-verification-steps, the third inefficient-navigation-attempts (cycling through tabs or menus, repeatedly opening wrong links). One code-book example is a web surfer that keeps failing searches without changing the query. The paper gives the distribution only as a figure. — [Magentic-One paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.04468)
- Known cost of the reset: on WebArena the authors report the agents had to discover and rediscover solutions to sub-tasks repeatedly because insights are not carried over. — [Magentic-One paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.04468)

**OpenHands (stuck detector, legacy controller and 2026 SDK)**
- Five scenarios in both versions: (1) the same action followed by the same observation 4 times; (2) the same action followed by an error 3 times; (3) agent monologue, 3 agent messages in a row; (4) an alternating A,B,A,B,A,B pattern across the last 6 actions and 6 observations; (5) a context-window error loop, 10 consecutive condensation events (legacy; stubbed out in the SDK). — [OpenHands legacy `stuck.py`](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/1.0.0/openhands/controller/stuck.py), [OpenHands SDK `stuck_detector.py`](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/main/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/conversation/stuck_detector.py)
- SDK defaults, exact: `action_observation=4`, `action_error=3`, `monologue=3`, `alternating_pattern=6`; the scan window is the last 20 events after the most recent user message. — [OpenHands SDK `types.py`](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/main/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/conversation/types.py)
- The SDK escalates in two steps. When the same call has errored exactly 3 times it injects one user-role message from the environment, once per streak. Paraphrase: you called this tool with the same arguments 3 times in a row and got the same error each time (error text included); repeating the identical call will not work, so read the error and either correct the arguments or try a different approach. On one more repeat (streak greater than 3) `is_stuck()` returns true, the conversation status is set to STUCK and the run loop stops. — [OpenHands SDK `stuck_detector.py`](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/main/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/conversation/stuck_detector.py), [OpenHands SDK `local_conversation.py`](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/main/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/conversation/impl/local_conversation.py)
- In the SDK, two action events count as equal only if source, tool name, action arguments and the thought text all match. A model that rewords its thought while sending the same call is not detected. — [OpenHands SDK `stuck_detector.py`](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/main/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/conversation/stuck_detector.py)
- The legacy detector records a stuck analysis with the loop type, the repeat count and the history index where the loop started. — [OpenHands legacy `stuck.py`](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/1.0.0/openhands/controller/stuck.py)

**Gemini CLI (Google, loop detection service)**
- Tool-call loop: each call is hashed as SHA-256 of name plus JSON arguments. `TOOL_CALL_LOOP_THRESHOLD = 5`. The check is not only for consecutive identical calls: for every cycle length k from 1 to 5 it tests whether the last k calls repeat 5 times (so k times 5 calls of history). — [gemini-cli `loopDetectionService.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/packages/core/src/services/loopDetectionService.ts)
- Content "chanting" loop: the streamed text is cut into sliding 50-character chunks; a loop is declared when one chunk occurs 10 times (`CONTENT_LOOP_THRESHOLD = 10`) with an average gap of at most 250 characters and the text between occurrences has at most 5 distinct forms. Code blocks are excluded, and tables, lists and headings reset the tracker to avoid false positives. — [gemini-cli `loopDetectionService.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/packages/core/src/services/loopDetectionService.ts)
- LLM-judged loop: after 30 turns within one prompt, every 10 turns by default (interval adapts between 5 and 15 with confidence), a cheap model reads the last 20 history items and returns a confidence between 0 and 1; a loop is declared at 0.9 or higher and is double-checked by a second model. The judge prompt requires both a repetitive pattern over at least 5 consecutive model actions and no net progress, and lists what is not a loop: the same tool on different files, incremental edits, sequential reads, and retry with variation. It instructs the judge to compare arguments, not tool names. — [gemini-cli `loopDetectionService.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/packages/core/src/services/loopDetectionService.ts)
- Recovery: on the first detection the client clears the flag, injects one feedback message and runs another turn. Paraphrase: system notice of a potential loop with the detail (the repeated call or text), a request to step back and confirm forward progress, and if there is none to analyse previous actions, rethink the approach, and avoid repeating tool calls or responses that bring no new result. The detection count is kept so a second detection is treated as count 2. — [gemini-cli `client.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/packages/core/src/core/client.ts)

**Browser Use (2026 main branch)**
- `ActionLoopDetector` keeps a rolling window of 20 action hashes and counts the most repeated hash. Nudges escalate when the count reaches 5, 8 and 12. A page-stagnation nudge fires when the page fingerprint is identical for 5 consecutive steps. The class docstring says the system is soft and "never blocks actions". — [browser-use `views.py`](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/blob/main/browser_use/agent/views.py)
- Hash normalisation: search queries are lower-cased, stripped of punctuation and reduced to a sorted token set, so reordered keywords collide; clicks hash by element index; inputs by index plus lower-cased text; navigation by full URL; scroll by direction and index. — [browser-use `views.py`](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/blob/main/browser_use/agent/views.py)
- Page fingerprint: URL, element count, and the first 16 hex characters of SHA-256 of the DOM text. — [browser-use `views.py`](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/blob/main/browser_use/agent/views.py)
- Nudge wording (paraphrase): opens as a casual heads-up, states that a similar action was repeated N times in the last M actions, and explicitly allows the agent to carry on if the repetition is intentional and productive, otherwise suggests reconsidering. The stagnation nudge says the page content has not changed across N consecutive actions, the actions may not be having the intended effect, and a different element or approach may be worth trying. — [browser-use `views.py`](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/blob/main/browser_use/agent/views.py)
- Other controls: a replan nudge after 3 consecutive failed steps (`planning_replan_on_stall = 3`) asking for a revised plan; a planning nudge after 5 steps without a plan; `max_failures = 5` consecutive failures then a forced final "done" call; a budget warning at 75% of the step budget telling the agent to consolidate and finish with partial results. — [browser-use `service.py`](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/blob/main/browser_use/agent/service.py)
- Multi-action batches are cut short: actions flagged as sequence-terminating (navigate, search, go back, switch tab) end the batch, and if the page changed after an action the remaining actions are skipped and logged. — [browser-use `service.py`](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/blob/main/browser_use/agent/service.py)

**Reflexion (2023, background)**
- Trigger heuristic in the AlfWorld experiments: self-reflect if the agent executes the same action and receives the same response for more than 3 cycles, or if the trial exceeds 30 actions. Memory holds the last 1 to 3 reflections. — [Reflexion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.11366)
- Effect: 130 of 134 AlfWorld tasks solved; +22% over baselines in AlfWorld. Limitation: on WebShop the runs were stopped after four trials with no improvement, and the authors conclude the method cannot solve tasks needing much diversity and exploration; it can settle in local minima. — [Reflexion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.11366)

**ReAct failure analysis (2022, background)**
- In the HotpotQA error analysis, 47% of ReAct failures are reasoning errors, a category that includes the model repetitively generating its previous thoughts and actions and failing to leave the loop. A footnote suspects greedy decoding as the cause. Another 23% are non-informative search results. — [ReAct](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629)

**Agent-E (2024)**
- Change observation: after every action the skill reports what changed, using code only (watching attributes such as aria-expanded and a DOM Mutation Observer). The feedback is a sentence in the action result, for example that an element was clicked and as a consequence a popup with certain elements appeared. The authors describe it as similar to Reflexion but not tied to a prior failure and not LLM-generated. — [Agent-E](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.13032)
- Hierarchy: a planner delegates one sub-task at a time to a browser navigation agent that is freshly instantiated for each sub-task (no carried chat history) and reports success or failure; the planner can then write a new plan or add a backtracking step such as returning to a results URL. — [Agent-E](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.13032)
- Results: 73.2% on WebVoyager; 26.9% failures, of which 14.1 points were self-aware and 12.8 points oblivious; about 25 LLM calls per task; about 150 s per successful and 220 s per failed task. No ablation isolates change observation. — [Agent-E](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.13032)

**AgentOccam (2024)**
- WebArena success 43.1% with GPT-4-Turbo against 37.2% for WebPilot, 35.5% for AWM, 33.3% for a SteP replication and 16.5% for the vanilla agent. — [AgentOccam](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.13825)
- Cumulative ablation on a 190-task dev subset, GPT-4-Turbo then Gemini-1.5-Flash: vanilla 14.2 / 11.6; reduced action space 25.8 / 23.2; scrolling disabled (full page loaded) 30.0 / 24.2; simplified observation 34.7 / 30.0; selective history replay 36.8 / 32.1; planning with branch and prune 44.2 / 33.7. — [AgentOccam](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.13825)
- The authors observe that LLM policies scroll up and down when they do not know what to do, which causes looping, and that selective history replay lets the agent avoid repetitive actions. The prune action lets the agent abandon a failing plan branch; steps and observations of dropped plans are removed from the window. — [AgentOccam](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.13825)

**SWE-agent (2024)**
- History processor: observations older than the last 5 are each collapsed to one line. Ablation on SWE-bench Lite with GPT-4 Turbo: last-5 observations 18.0% resolved, full history 15.0%. — [SWE-agent](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15793)
- Guardrail: an edit that introduces a lint error is reverted and not applied; the agent is shown the error, what the edit would have produced, and the original file. The rejection opens with "Your changes have NOT been applied." Without the linter guardrail, 15.0% against 18.0%. — [SWE-agent](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15793)
- Cascade statistic: any edit has a 90.5% chance of eventually succeeding, falling to 57.2% after a single failed edit; 23.4% of unresolved trajectories were labelled cascading failed edits. Resolved runs took a median 12 steps, unresolved runs averaged 21 steps. — [SWE-agent](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15793)

**Failure taxonomies**
- MAST (1,642 annotated multi-agent traces, 7 frameworks): step repetition is reported at 15.7% of observed failures, the largest single mode. This figure came from search excerpts of the paper and secondary summaries; I did not see the table itself. — [MAST](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.13657)
- WorkArena++ error analysis (GPT-4o and Llama3): when an action does not change the page state, models tend to retry the same action instead of trying another approach, and they often hallucinate the consequences of their actions, believing progress was made. Agents also get confused by element ids, so a click lands on a wrong element or errors without effect. From a search excerpt of the paper. — [WorkArena++](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.05291)
- StressWeb (2026): 58.4% of trajectories contain exact repeated actions even in the clean environment, and under perturbation the longest run reaches 92 consecutive identical actions. From a search excerpt only. — [StressWeb](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.16385)

**Not re-fetched in this session (recalled; verify before citing)**
- LATS combines Monte-Carlo tree search over actions with an LLM value function and reflection, and requires reverting the environment to earlier states. — [LATS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.04406)
- WebPilot uses an MCTS-inspired planner with explorer, verifier, appraiser and reflection roles. — [WebPilot](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.15978)
- SteP composes a stack of hand-written, site-specific policies. AgentOccam reports that such hints can mislead the agent when they do not fit the task. — [SteP](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.03720), [AgentOccam](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.13825)

### Inferences
- The 78-click and 65-step failures would have been stopped by any of the four code-level detectors within 3 to 12 steps. The gap in the hackathon system is not detection sensitivity but what happens after detection.
- Magentic-One's design choice worth copying is the pairing of a counter that decays on progress with a recovery that discards every agent's context and re-seeds it from a ledger. Its design choice not worth copying for a 3-second non-thinking model is letting the model judge its own progress each round: that costs one extra call per round and depends on exactly the self-awareness that is missing (see MIRAGE-Bench in section 2).
- LATS and WebPilot style tree search is impractical here: live stateful sites cannot be reverted and the run has 20 minutes. Their transferable idea is small: sample several candidate actions and let an evaluator pick one.
- SteP's site-specific policies are both forbidden by the competition rules and reported as brittle.

### Gaps
- Magentic-UI was not researched; I found no source describing changes to its stall logic.
- BrowserGym/AgentLab: no published per-model loop rates were found; the WorkArena++ analysis is qualitative.
- What Gemini CLI does on the second detection was not read (only the comment that the count is preserved).
- The default `max_stalls = 3` in the AutoGen team class is recalled from the API, consistent with the paper's "exceeds 2", but not re-read.
- No ablation exists that isolates the stall counter or the context reset in Magentic-One (only the whole ledger orchestrator).

## 2. Why do small or non-reasoning models repeat, and which context/history designs reduce it?

### Takeaway
Repetition is self-reinforcing: each copy of a thought or action in the context raises the probability of the next copy, and small instruct models loop far more than large or reasoning ones while being confident about it. The designs with measured benefit are structural: fewer actions, shorter and selective history, results instead of raw old observations, and explicit state-change feedback. LLM-written summaries of history did not help small models.

### Cited Findings
- Self-reinforcement (2022, background): language models prefer to repeat the previous sentence; the more often a sentence already appears in the context, the more likely it is generated again; sentences with higher initial probability reinforce more strongly. — [Xu et al., Learning to Break the Loop](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.02369)
- ReAct (2022, background) saw the model regenerate its previous thought and action and suspected greedy decoding. — [ReAct](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629)
- Manus engineering write-up (2025): models imitate the pattern of behaviour present in their context; when the context is full of similar action-observation pairs the model keeps following the pattern even when it stops being useful. Their countermeasure is controlled variation in how actions and observations are serialised (different templates, phrasing, minor noise in order or formatting). — [Manus, Context Engineering for AI Agents](https://manus.im/blog/Context-Engineering-for-AI-Agents-Lessons-from-Building-Manus)
- Same write-up: failed actions and their error output should stay in the context, because seeing the failure shifts the model away from similar actions; erasing failures removes the evidence. A constantly rewritten todo list recites the goal at the end of the context to counter drift across roughly 50 tool calls. — [Manus, Context Engineering for AI Agents](https://manus.im/blog/Context-Engineering-for-AI-Agents-Lessons-from-Building-Manus)
- TIDE (2026) defines Loop Ratio as the share of actions that are redundant loop steps, found by hashing environment states (exact text match; for screenshots CLIP similarity at 0.999). A single action that leaves the state unchanged counts as a cycle. — [TIDE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.02196)
- TIDE loop ratios on WebShop: Qwen3-4B-Instruct 36.7%, Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct 5.7%, Mistral-7B-Instruct 17.5%, Phi-4 2.6%, Gemini 2.5 Flash 0.2%, DeepSeek-V3.2 0.0%. Thinking variants: Qwen3-4B-Thinking 4.5% and Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking 0.7% on WebShop, but Qwen3-4B-Thinking loops more than the instruct variant on BlocksWorld (28.5% against 15.8%) and Sudoku (34.3% against 22.5%), and Phi-4-reasoning reaches 35.7% on WebShop. — [TIDE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.02196)
- TIDE explanation: agents persist in recursive failure rather than adapting to negative feedback; action entropy is low on loop steps, so the agent is confidently fixated on the wrong path. The paper states loop mitigation is an unresolved challenge. — [TIDE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.02196)
- TIDE on memory: full history is often a burden for open-weight models in reasoning-bound tasks (for example a memory index of -21.9 for Phi-4-reasoning on FrozenLake) but helps in partially observable tasks such as WebShop. With a sliding window, gains come almost entirely from the first 5 turns and then plateau. LLM summarisation of memory did not help Qwen3-4B-Instruct: its score fell on BlocksWorld (30.8 to 23.5), Sudoku (19.3 to 11.9) and WebShop (9.6 to 4.8). — [TIDE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.02196)
- MIRAGE-Bench (2025) builds WebArena snapshots at the third and the sixth repetition of an invalid action and scores the next step: 2 if the agent acknowledges the repetition and tries to fix it, 1 if it changes course without acknowledging, 0 if it repeats unaware. The authors chose the third repetition because three identical attempts already exceed normal human trial and error. Rate of the bad outcome in the repetitive-history setting: Claude-3.5-Sonnet 0.227, Qwen2.5-72B 0.312, Qwen2.5-32B 0.330, Gemini-2.5-flash 0.333, GPT-4o 0.345, Qwen2.5-7B 0.351, GPT-4o-mini 0.435, Llama-3.1-70B 0.591. — [MIRAGE-Bench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.21017)
- WorkArena++: a no-effect action is retried, and consequences are hallucinated (from a search excerpt). — [WorkArena++](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.05291)
- AgentOccam: removing actions the model overuses when lost (scroll, noop, tab operations, hover, press) and loading the full page gave the largest gains; selective history replay added about 2 points and is credited with avoiding repeated actions; a longer history raises context length and reasoning difficulty. For Gemini-1.5-Flash the planning prompt added only 1.6 points, whereas action-space reduction added 11.6. — [AgentOccam](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.13825)
- SWE-agent: collapsing all but the last 5 observations beat full history by 3 points; the stated reason includes not showing outdated file information. — [SWE-agent](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15793)
- Anthropic (2025): recall degrades as context grows; context is a finite attention budget with diminishing returns; clearing old tool results is the safest light form of compaction; structured notes kept outside the context let an agent continue coherently after a context reset. — [Anthropic, Effective context engineering for AI agents](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents)
- An unreviewed research note argues that looping in terminal agents is a gradual collapse of action entropy that begins tens to hundreds of turns before visible repetition. Blog-level source; from a search excerpt only. — [Research note on looping dynamics](https://torpid-telephone-b59.notion.site/REDACTED)

### Inferences
- The hackathon history format is close to a worst case for self-reinforcement. The last 2 turns are verbatim, including the model's own thought, and older turns are compressed to action results. In a loop, the verbatim window holds two copies of the same thought and the compressed tail holds dozens of identical result lines. That is a few-shot prompt for producing the same turn again. The "X has stroke 500, not 507" case fits exactly: the stale sentence was re-read from the agent's own previous output each turn and outweighed the corrected shared state.
- With thinking off and low temperature the model is near-deterministic: an almost identical prompt yields an identical turn. A static warning string that is itself identical every turn does not change this; it becomes part of the repeated pattern. This explains why the injected three-times warning was ignored.
- Recommended history design, ranked by expected effect for a small model: (a) never replay the model's own thought text; store only harness-written results; (b) collapse repeated attempts into one ledger line with a count and an outcome, which keeps the failure evidence (Manus) while removing the repeated pattern (Xu, Manus); (c) add a code-computed change line after every action (Agent-E) so a no-effect action is labelled as such instead of being left for the model to infer (WorkArena++); (d) show what changed in the shared case file since the agent's last turn, at the end of the prompt; (e) keep the verbatim window short (TIDE: little gain beyond 5 turns; SWE-agent: last 5).
- Build any hand-over or reset summary in code from structured ledgers. TIDE's result that LLM summarisation lowered small-model scores argues against asking the same small model to summarise its own failed trajectory.
- Turning thinking mode on is not a reliable cure by itself (TIDE: mixed for 4B, helpful at 30B). Using it for a single post-mortem call after a stall is plausible but untested here.
- Raising temperature for the one call after a block should increase diversity because loop steps are low-entropy (TIDE) and greedy decoding was already suspected in ReAct. No source measured this for agents.

### Gaps
- No source measures the effect of removing the previous thought from history, of a tabu list, or of showing a page diff instead of the page, in isolation. The recommendations combine adjacent evidence.
- No published loop data for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next; the closest are Qwen3 4B and 30B-A3B in TIDE and Qwen2.5 in MIRAGE-Bench.
- MIRAGE-Bench does not report the third and sixth repetition separately in the text that was readable.

## 3. Hard interventions versus soft hints: what works and what are the failure modes?

### Takeaway
Soft hints are the industry default and the weakest lever: models that are already repeating continue to do so unaware in roughly a quarter to more than half of cases. The measured wins come from hard structure: rejecting the invalid action with a factual result, removing or masking actions, and resetting to a fresh context seeded from a ledger. Hard measures fail by blocking legitimate repetition, by losing knowledge on reset, and by pushing the agent into a neighbouring useless action.

### Cited Findings
- Soft only: Browser Use states its detector generates context messages and never blocks; its wording explicitly permits continuing. — [browser-use `views.py`](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/blob/main/browser_use/agent/views.py)
- Soft then different handling: Gemini CLI injects one feedback message on the first detection and keeps the count for a second detection. — [gemini-cli `client.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/packages/core/src/core/client.ts)
- Nudge then halt: OpenHands SDK nudges once at 3 identical erroring calls and stops the run with status STUCK on the next; it does not recover by itself. — [OpenHands SDK `local_conversation.py`](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/main/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/conversation/impl/local_conversation.py)
- Evidence that visible repetition alone does not stop repetition: with 3 or 6 repeats in the history, models repeat unaware in 22.7% to 59.1% of MIRAGE-Bench snapshots (35.1% for Qwen2.5-7B, 43.5% for GPT-4o-mini). — [MIRAGE-Bench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.21017)
- Hard rejection with a factual result: SWE-agent's linter refuses the edit, says it was not applied and shows the current state; +3 points. Without recovery the failure cascades: success probability falls from 90.5% to 57.2% after one failed edit. — [SWE-agent](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15793)
- Removing actions outright: AgentOccam's action-space reduction and disabling of scroll are its largest gains, and they hold for a small fast model (Gemini-1.5-Flash 11.6 to 24.2). — [AgentOccam](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.13825)
- Constraining the choice at decoding time: Manus masks token logits or prefills the response so the model must call a tool, or must pick from a subset of tools, instead of editing the tool list or adding instructions. — [Manus, Context Engineering for AI Agents](https://manus.im/blog/Context-Engineering-for-AI-Agents-Lessons-from-Building-Manus)
- Reset with fresh context: Magentic-One clears all agent contexts on every replan and re-seeds from the updated ledger (the ledger orchestrator as a whole is worth 31%). Agent-E gives every sub-task a newly instantiated navigation agent. Anthropic recommends sub-agents with clean context windows that return a condensed summary of about 1,000 to 2,000 tokens. — [Magentic-One paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.04468), [Agent-E](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.13032), [Anthropic, Effective context engineering for AI agents](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents)
- Failure mode of resets: knowledge is lost and sub-task solutions are rediscovered repeatedly (Magentic-One on WebArena). — [Magentic-One paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.04468)
- Failure mode of LLM-written summaries for small models: scores dropped with summarised memory. — [TIDE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.02196)
- Failure mode of reflection: Reflexion did not improve WebShop and can stay in local minima when the reflections are not useful. — [Reflexion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.11366)
- Failure mode of over-eager detection: Gemini CLI's judge prompt and content tracker carry explicit exclusions for batch work over different targets, incremental edits, sequential reads and retry with variation, because these look like loops. — [gemini-cli `loopDetectionService.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/packages/core/src/services/loopDetectionService.ts)
- Failure mode of exact matching: OpenHands SDK equality includes the thought text, so a reworded thought hides the loop; Browser Use normalises search tokens for this reason. — [OpenHands SDK `stuck_detector.py`](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/main/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/conversation/stuck_detector.py), [browser-use `views.py`](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/blob/main/browser_use/agent/views.py)
- Hybrid detection beats either kind alone in one study: on 1,575 trajectories a combination of structural and semantic cycle detection reached F1 0.72 against 0.08 structural-only and 0.28 semantic-only. From a search excerpt only. — [Unsupervised Cycle Detection in Agentic Applications](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.10650)

### Inferences
- A refusal alone converts a wasted action into a no-op; it does not make the model move. The 78-click case would become 78 refusals. Refusals must count as stalls and drive an escalation: block, then forced choice among alternatives, then reset, then park the question.
- A tabu entry must be keyed on the action together with the page state it was tried on, and created only when the outcome was an error or no change. Then paging through a list (same button, different page each time) is never blocked, which answers the legitimate-repetition failure mode.
- After a block the agent may alternate between two useless actions. Cycle detection over turn signatures plus the stall counter catches this and escalates to a reset.
- Forced choice by a second model fits the competition rules as long as the candidates are proposed by the navigation model and only filtered by code (validation and blocking are allowed; enumeration and trying of links by code would be crawling). The decision model's known weakness is unknown here; always include generic escape options (go back, start page, give up on this question for now).
- Resetting should keep the tabu list and the attempt ledger across the reset, otherwise the fresh agent repeats the dead ends (the Magentic-One rediscovery problem).
- Handing a sub-goal to another agent is the same mechanism as a reset with a brief, plus a different site. It is useful only if the open question can be answered elsewhere; otherwise parking the question and finishing with a flagged gap protects the time budget.

### Gaps
- No source measures refusal-plus-forced-choice against a nudge for loop recovery, and none evaluates a separate decision model as the chooser. This is the least evidenced part of the recommendation.
- No data on how many resets are worthwhile before giving up; Magentic-One only bounds total rounds or time.

## 4. Detection signals beyond exact repetition: which are used in practice and with what thresholds?

### Takeaway
Production detectors use five signals: identical action (3 to 5), identical action plus identical observation (4), short cycles (period up to 5, 3 to 5 repeats), unchanged page fingerprint (5 steps), and repeated text or monologue (3 messages, or 10 repeated chunks). Progress-based signals (no new facts) appear only in LLM-judged form (Magentic-One) or as step budgets. A system with a recomputed list of open questions can make the progress signal deterministic, which none of the cited systems can.

### Cited Findings

| Signal | Used by | Threshold | Response |
|---|---|---|---|
| Same action, same error | OpenHands SDK | 3 nudge, 4 halt | message, then STUCK |
| Same action, same observation | OpenHands; Reflexion | 4; more than 3 cycles | halt; reflect |
| Same tool call, exact hash | Gemini CLI | 5 consecutive | feedback turn |
| Cycle of period k | Gemini CLI; OpenHands | k = 1..5 repeated 5 times; A,B over 6 steps | feedback turn; halt |
| Similar action in rolling window | Browser Use | 5 / 8 / 12 of last 20 (normalised hash) | escalating nudge |
| Unchanged page fingerprint | Browser Use; TIDE (metric) | 5 consecutive steps; any no-change action counts as a cycle | nudge; metric only |
| Repeated text / monologue | OpenHands; Gemini CLI | 3 agent messages; a 50-char chunk 10 times | halt; feedback turn |
| Consecutive failed steps | Browser Use | 3 replan nudge, 5 forced finish | nudge; forced done |
| No forward progress (LLM-judged) | Magentic-One | counter +1 per stalled round, -1 per good round, replan at 3 | reset and replan |
| LLM loop judge | Gemini CLI | after 30 turns, every 5 to 15 turns, confidence 0.9, two models | feedback turn |
| Step or time budget | Browser Use; Reflexion; Magentic-One | 75% warning; 30 actions; max rounds or time | wrap up; reflect; final answer |

Sources: [OpenHands SDK `stuck_detector.py`](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/main/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/conversation/stuck_detector.py), [OpenHands SDK `types.py`](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/main/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/conversation/types.py), [gemini-cli `loopDetectionService.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/packages/core/src/services/loopDetectionService.ts), [browser-use `views.py`](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/blob/main/browser_use/agent/views.py), [browser-use `service.py`](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/blob/main/browser_use/agent/service.py), [autogen `_magentic_one_orchestrator.py`](https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/blob/main/python/packages/autogen-agentchat/src/autogen_agentchat/teams/_group_chat/_magentic_one/_magentic_one_orchestrator.py), [Reflexion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.11366), [TIDE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.02196)

- MIRAGE-Bench treats the third identical attempt as already beyond normal human trial and error. — [MIRAGE-Bench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.21017)
- StressWeb reports runs of up to 92 consecutive identical actions (search excerpt only), the same order as the 78-click failure. — [StressWeb](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.16385)

### Inferences
- Thresholds in coding agents (4 to 5) are set for sessions of hundreds of steps with a human present. For a 20-minute unattended run at about 3 s per call, lower them: refuse the third identical no-effect action, flag a cycle at 2 repeats of the period (3 for period 1), flag stagnation at 3 turns.
- Mapping the four observed failures to signals: the 78 clicks on a vanished element are caught before execution by validating the target against the current page (no counting needed); the 4-query cycle is caught by period-4 cycle detection at step 8 and by the rolling-window count; the 46-turn repeated search with the same thought is caught by the no-effect count at turn 3 and by thought similarity; the mailbox reloads are caught by an unchanged fingerprint after a navigation action.
- "No new evidence in N steps" needs novelty measured by content hash, otherwise re-filing the same page counts as progress. Visiting a never-seen page is weaker evidence of progress than a new fact; it should slow the stall counter, not reset it.
- Time since last progress is better used as a per-question budget (park the question when spent) than as a stall trigger, because it would otherwise fire on every turn once exceeded.

### Gaps
- No published thresholds for thought-similarity (Jaccard or embedding) in agents; the 0.8 token-overlap value proposed below is a guess.
- No source uses "open questions closed" as a progress signal; this is specific to the hackathon system.

## 5. How do strong systems phrase an intervention so the model changes course?

### Takeaway
The interventions with measured benefit read as environment results, not advice: they state that the action was not carried out, give the specific evidence, show the current state, and demand a different next step. The widely used advisory nudges are permissive by design and are the kind the hackathon agent already ignored.

### Cited Findings
- SWE-agent's rejection is a result, not a hint: the change was not applied, here is the error, here is what the edit would have produced, here is the unchanged file, fix the command and retry. — [SWE-agent](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15793)
- OpenHands' nudge names the tool, the count (3), the identical error text, states flatly that the same call will not work, and offers two exits: correct the arguments or change approach. It is sent as a user-role message from the environment, once per streak, to avoid the nudge itself repeating. — [OpenHands SDK `stuck_detector.py`](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/main/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/conversation/stuck_detector.py)
- Magentic-One asks for the root cause before the new plan, and asks specifically for a plan that avoids repeating the same mistakes; it also forces at least one new or updated guess in the fact sheet, which pushes the model to state a different hypothesis. The next instruction to each agent is written fresh by the orchestrator and addressed directly to that agent with the specific information it needs. — [autogen `_prompts.py`](https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/blob/main/python/packages/autogen-agentchat/src/autogen_agentchat/teams/_group_chat/_magentic_one/_prompts.py)
- Gemini CLI includes the concrete detail of what repeated (the call and its arguments, or the repeated text) in the feedback. — [gemini-cli `client.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/packages/core/src/core/client.ts)
- Browser Use's nudges are deliberately non-directive: they allow the agent to continue if it believes it is progressing. Its budget warning is directive and ordered: consolidate results, then finish, because partial results beat none. — [browser-use `views.py`](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/blob/main/browser_use/agent/views.py), [browser-use `service.py`](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/blob/main/browser_use/agent/service.py)
- Browser Use's normal output schema has the model evaluate the previous goal before stating the next goal; its fast mode drops both fields and thinking. — [browser-use `views.py`](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/blob/main/browser_use/agent/views.py)
- MIRAGE-Bench's best outcome requires explicit acknowledgement of the repetition, not just a different action. — [MIRAGE-Bench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.21017)
- Agent-E attaches the consequence of each action to the action result in plain language. — [Agent-E](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.13032)
- Manus keeps goals at the end of the context by recitation and varies serialisation so the model does not lock onto a template. — [Manus, Context Engineering for AI Agents](https://manus.im/blog/Context-Engineering-for-AI-Agents-Lessons-from-Building-Manus)

### Inferences
Rules for wording an intervention for a small non-thinking model:
1. Put it where the action result goes, as the last thing before the reply, and start with the outcome in capitals: NOT EXECUTED.
2. State facts with numbers taken from the ledger: which action, how many times, what each result was, what the page is now. No "consider" or "might".
3. State the consequence as a property of the environment: this action is refused until the page changes.
4. Remove the old thought from the context in the same turn; otherwise the hint competes with two verbatim copies of the belief it contradicts.
5. Shrink the reply space: offer lettered options and accept only a letter, or require a field that names what will be different. Require the model to restate the last result in its own reply before the thought (an acknowledgement field), mirroring the evaluate-previous-step field.
6. Never send the same intervention text twice in a row: include the changing count and the specific action, and escalate to a structurally different step (forced choice, reset) rather than repeating a warning.
7. On reset, tell the new context it is taking over from a stopped investigator and give the reason for the stop as a fact.

### Gaps
- No controlled comparison of intervention wordings was found; the rules above are derived from which systems report gains and from the failure already observed in the hackathon runs.

## 6. Concrete algorithms to add to an existing Python observe-think-act loop

### Takeaway
Add one deterministic guard object per investigator with four parts: a gate before each action (stale target, tabu), a change line after each action, a stall counter fed by deterministic progress signals, and a three-step escalation (block, forced choice by the decision model, restart from a code-built brief), ending in parking the question. All choices of where to go remain with the models; code only validates, blocks, restarts and reports.

### Cited Findings (design basis)
- Stall counter with decay and replan at 3; full context reset on replan. — [autogen `_magentic_one_orchestrator.py`](https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/blob/main/python/packages/autogen-agentchat/src/autogen_agentchat/teams/_group_chat/_magentic_one/_magentic_one_orchestrator.py)
- Cycle detection over periods 1 to 5 on hashed calls. — [gemini-cli `loopDetectionService.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/packages/core/src/services/loopDetectionService.ts)
- Token-sorted search normalisation, page fingerprint, rolling window of 20, batch cut when the page changes. — [browser-use `views.py`](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/blob/main/browser_use/agent/views.py), [browser-use `service.py`](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/blob/main/browser_use/agent/service.py)
- Identical action plus error at 3, action plus observation at 4, alternating at 6. — [OpenHands SDK `types.py`](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/main/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/conversation/types.py)
- Code-computed change observation in the action result. — [Agent-E](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.13032)
- Rejecting an invalid action with a factual result; last-5 observation window. — [SWE-agent](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15793)
- Keep failures visible, vary serialisation, constrain the choice instead of advising. — [Manus, Context Engineering for AI Agents](https://manus.im/blog/Context-Engineering-for-AI-Agents-Lessons-from-Building-Manus)
- LLM summaries hurt small models; window gains saturate by 5 turns. — [TIDE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.02196)

### Inferences

Everything below is my design. Thresholds are starting values to tune on recorded runs.

**A. Signatures and fingerprint**

```python
import hashlib, re
from collections import Counter, deque

_W = re.compile(r"\w+")
def _norm(s):   return " ".join(_W.findall((s or "").lower()))
def _tokset(s): return frozenset(_W.findall((s or "").lower()))

def page_fp(url, a11y_text):
    """What the model can see, minus volatile clock times."""
    t = re.sub(r"\b\d{1,2}:\d{2}(:\d{2})?\b", "", a11y_text)
    return hashlib.sha256((url.split("#")[0] + "|" + _norm(t)).encode()).hexdigest()[:16]

def action_sig(a, elements):
    """Survives renumbered element ids and reordered query words."""
    k = a["kind"]
    if k in ("click", "fill"):
        el = elements.get(a.get("target"))
        who = f"{el['role']}:{_norm(el['name'])}" if el else f"gone:{a.get('target')}"
        val = " ".join(sorted(_tokset(a.get("value")))) if k == "fill" else ""
        return f"{k}|{who}|{val}"
    if k == "goto":
        return "goto|" + a["url"].split("#")[0]
    return k + "|" + _norm(str(a.get("target", "")))
```

**B. The guard**

```python
class StallGuard:
    BLOCK_AFTER = 2     # same action on the same page with no effect or an error: the 3rd is refused
    WINDOW      = 12    # turns kept for cycle and frequency checks
    FREQ        = 4     # same signature 4 times in WINDOW without a gain
    IDLE_LIMIT  = 6     # idle points before a stall (new page without a gain costs 0.5, else 1)
    MAX_STALLS  = 3     # Magentic-One value
    MAX_RESETS  = 2

    def __init__(self):
        self.dead    = Counter()             # (fp_before, sig) -> error / no-effect count
        self.ledger  = {}                    # (fp_before, sig) -> {"desc", "n", "outcome"}
        self.turns   = deque(maxlen=self.WINDOW)
        self.thoughts = deque(maxlen=4)
        self.seen    = set()
        self.stalls = 0; self.resets = 0; self.idle = 0.0

    # before every single action
    def gate(self, a, cur, seen_elements):
        """cur: live page; seen_elements: the elements the model saw when it wrote this turn."""
        fp, sig = page_fp(cur.url, cur.text), action_sig(a, cur.elements)
        if a["kind"] in ("click", "fill"):
            now, then = cur.elements.get(a["target"]), seen_elements.get(a["target"])
            if now is None or then is None or (now["role"], now["name"]) != (then["role"], then["name"]):
                return False, sig, "stale"       # target vanished or id now means something else
        if self.dead[(fp, sig)] >= self.BLOCK_AFTER:
            return False, sig, "blocked"
        return True, sig, None

    # after every executed action
    def record(self, sig, fp_before, fp_after, error, desc, gained=False):
        effect = (not error) and (fp_after != fp_before or gained)
        if not effect:
            self.dead[(fp_before, sig)] += 1
        e = self.ledger.setdefault((fp_before, sig), {"desc": desc, "n": 0, "outcome": ""})
        e["n"] += 1
        e["outcome"] = error or ("page changed" if fp_after != fp_before else
                                 "new evidence" if gained else "nothing changed")
        return effect

    # once per turn
    def end_turn(self, sigs, effects, thought, gained, fp_after):
        """gained: a fact slot was filled or changed, an open question closed,
        or evidence with a never-seen content hash was filed."""
        self.turns.append(tuple(sigs))
        novel = fp_after not in self.seen; self.seen.add(fp_after)
        why = []
        if not any(effects):                          why.append("no action had any effect")
        k = _cycle(list(self.turns))
        if k:                                         why.append(f"the last turns repeat with period {k}")
        flat = Counter(s for t in self.turns for s in t)
        if flat and max(flat.values()) >= self.FREQ:  why.append("one action sent 4+ times in 12 turns")
        if _same_thought(self.thoughts, thought):     why.append("same thought as an earlier turn")
        if gained:
            self.idle = 0.0; self.stalls = 0
            return []
        self.idle += 0.5 if novel else 1.0
        if self.idle >= self.IDLE_LIMIT:              why.append("no new fact or evidence for a while")
        if why:
            self.stalls += 1
        return why

def _cycle(seq, max_k=4):
    n = len(seq)
    for k in range(1, max_k + 1):
        need = max(3, 2 * k)                  # AAA, ABAB, ABCABC, ABCDABCD
        if n >= need and all(seq[n - need + i] == seq[n - k + (i % k)] for i in range(need)):
            return k
    return 0

def _same_thought(prev, thought):
    t = _tokset(thought)
    hit = any(len(t & u) / max(1, len(t | u)) >= 0.8 for u in prev)
    prev.append(t)
    return hit
```

**C. The turn, with batch cut and escalation**

```python
def investigator_turn(agent, guard, case):
    if guard.stalls >= guard.MAX_STALLS:
        return restart_or_park(agent, guard, case)

    obs = agent.observe()                                   # url, text, elements, screenshot
    if guard.stalls == 2:
        thought, actions = "", [forced_choice(agent, guard, case, obs)]
    else:
        reply = agent.llm(build_prompt(agent, guard, case, obs),
                          temperature=0.2 if guard.stalls == 0 else 0.7)
        if reply.question not in case.open_ids():           # validation, not navigation
            agent.results = [f"NOT EXECUTED: {reply.question} is not open. " + case.why_closed(reply.question)]
            guard.end_turn([], [False], reply.thought, False, page_fp(obs.url, obs.text))
            return
        thought, actions = reply.thought, reply.actions

    sigs, effects, results = [], [], []
    for i, a in enumerate(actions):
        cur = agent.observe()
        ok, sig, why = guard.gate(a, cur, obs.elements)
        sigs.append(sig)
        if not ok:
            effects.append(False)
            results.append(refusal_text(a, why, cur, guard))
            if i < len(actions) - 1:
                results.append(f"SKIPPED the remaining {len(actions) - i - 1} action(s) of this turn.")
            break                                           # never run the rest of a batch blind
        fp0 = page_fp(cur.url, cur.text)
        err, gained = agent.execute(a)
        new = agent.observe(); fp1 = page_fp(new.url, new.text)
        effects.append(guard.record(sig, fp0, fp1, err, describe(a, cur), gained))
        results.append(change_line(a, cur, new, err))       # section D
        if err:
            break
    now = agent.observe()
    guard.end_turn(sigs, effects, thought, case.gained_since_last_turn(agent), page_fp(now.url, now.text))
    agent.results = results          # only results are stored; the thought is not replayed
```

```python
def forced_choice(agent, guard, case, obs):
    """Stall level 2. The navigation model proposes, code filters, the decision model picks."""
    fp = page_fp(obs.url, obs.text)
    q = case.focus_question(agent)
    banned = [e["desc"] for key, e in guard.ledger.items() if guard.dead[key] >= guard.BLOCK_AFTER]
    proposals = agent.llm_propose(question=q.text, page=obs.text, banned=banned,
                                  n=5, temperature=0.9, history=None)   # no history, no old thought
    cands, seen = [], set()
    for a in proposals:
        s = action_sig(a, obs.elements)
        if s in seen or guard.dead[(fp, s)] >= guard.BLOCK_AFTER or not is_valid(a, obs):
            continue
        seen.add(s); cands.append(a)
    cands += [GO_BACK, GOTO_START_PAGE, park_action(q)]     # generic exits, no site knowledge
    i = clef.pick(prompt=f"Open question: {q.text}\nWhich single next step is most likely to reveal the answer?",
                  options=[describe(a, obs) for a in cands], screenshots=[obs.screenshot])
    return cands[i]

def restart_or_park(agent, guard, case):
    """Stall level 3."""
    q = case.focus_question(agent)
    if guard.resets >= guard.MAX_RESETS:
        case.park(q, by=agent.name, tried=dead_ends(guard))   # visible to the form filler as a flagged gap
    else:
        agent.pinned = handover_brief(agent, guard, case)     # built by code from the ledgers
        agent.results = []                                    # every old turn and thought is dropped
        agent.goto(agent.start_url)                           # the entry URL given by the task
        guard.resets += 1
    guard.stalls = 0; guard.idle = 0.0
    guard.turns.clear(); guard.thoughts.clear()
    # guard.dead and guard.ledger are kept so the fresh context inherits the tabu list
```

**D. Change line after every action (code only)**

```python
def change_line(a, before, after, err):
    d = describe(a, before)
    if err:
        return f"FAILED: {d}. {err}"
    if after.url != before.url:
        return f"DONE: {d}. The browser is now on a different page: {after.title} ({after.url})."
    added   = [l for l in after.lines  if l not in before.line_set][:6]
    removed = [l for l in before.lines if l not in after.line_set][:3]
    if not added and not removed:
        return f"DONE: {d}. NOTHING CHANGED on the page."
    return f"DONE: {d}. Appeared: {added}. Disappeared: {removed}."
```

**E. Prompt layout (order matters; volatile facts last)**

```text
[system: role, action grammar]                                   static
[HANDOVER brief, only after a restart]
ATTEMPT LEDGER  (one line per distinct action+page, newest last, max 15)
   x1  search "<tokens>" on "<page title>"  -> 0 results
   x3  click button "<name>" on "<page title>"  -> nothing changed        [BLOCKED]
RESULTS OF YOUR LAST TURN  (results only, never the old thought)
CURRENT PAGE  (accessibility text)
PAGE STATUS: identical to last turn | changed: <added / removed lines>
CASE FILE CHANGES SINCE YOUR LAST TURN: <slot>: <old> -> <new> (by <agent>, mm:ss) | none
OPEN QUESTIONS  (recomputed now)
BLOCKED ACTIONS  (never executed while this page is unchanged)
Reply as: {"question": "<open question id>", "last_result": "<what the last result showed>",
           "thought": "<one sentence>", "actions": [...]}
```

Vary the wording of the two status lines between a few templates and always include the changing counts, so consecutive prompts are not token-identical.

**F. Intervention texts (my wording)**

```text
Refusal, stale target:
  NOT EXECUTED: click [e41] "Open tender". [e41] is not on the current page; it was on the page you
  saw 3 turns ago. The current page is "<title>" (<url>). Nothing was clicked. Use an element from
  CURRENT PAGE.

Refusal, tabu:
```

1. Gate plus batch cut plus change line (sections B gate, C loop, D). Removes the 78-click class entirely.
2. Stop replaying thoughts; deduplicated attempt ledger; case-file change line; question-id validation (section E).
3. Tabu on (page, action) with no-effect counting; cycle and frequency checks; stall counter.
4. Restart from a code-built brief; parking after two restarts.
5. Forced choice through the decision model (most novel, least evidenced; add last).

**Rule compliance.** The guard validates, blocks, restarts and reports. It never selects a link, a query or a document: proposals come from the navigation model and the pick from the decision model. P = lambda url, text, els: types.SimpleNamespace(url=url, text=text, elements=els)

def run(name, step, n=30):
    g = G(); first_block = first_stall = reset_at = None
    for t in range(1, n + 1):
        sigs, news, thought = step(g, t)

input.message:
Notes are saved at `D:\Personal_Projects\TUM_HackathonFinal\research_notes\Reliable multi site web agents\loop_and_stall_recovery.md` (not committed). They cover the five key questions plus a sixth section with pseudocode, each with Takeaway / Cited Findings / Inferences / Gaps.

**Two deviations from the brief**
- **Prompts are paraphrased, not quoted.** I worked under a limit on verbatim reproduction of source text, so each prompt and nudge is a close paraphrase with a link to the file holding the exact wording. Thresholds, field names and constants are exact.
- **About 30 tool calls instead of 15.** Firecrawl returned 429s and a low-credit warning after the first batch, so I switched to WebSearch/WebFetch and direct reads of the raw GitHub files.

**How solid the evidence is**
- Thresholds and control flow for Magentic-One (AutoGen), OpenHands (legacy and 2026 SDK), Gemini CLI and Browser Use were read directly from source on 2026-10-10.
- Paper numbers were extracted from arXiv HTML by the summarising fetch tool and not cross-checked against the PDFs.
- Three figures come from search excerpts only and are flagged in the notes: MAST step repetition 15.7%, StressWeb 58.4% of trajectories with repeats and runs of up to 92 identical actions, and the IBM cycle-detection F1 scores.
- LATS, WebPilot and SteP mechanisms are recalled, not re-fetched. Magentic-UI was not researched.

**Main findings**
- **Detection is not the gap; the response is.** All four code-level detectors would have caught the observed loops within 3 to 12 steps. They respond with a nudge (Browser Use says explicitly it does not block; Gemini CLI injects one feedback turn) or a halt (OpenHands nudges at 3 identical erroring calls, sets STUCK at 4). None refuses the action and forces an alternative.
- **Magentic-One is the one explicit replanner.** Its stall counter goes +1 on no progress or loop, -1 on a good round, and replans at 3. Replanning rewrites the fact sheet and plan (root cause first), then resets every agent's context. The paper reports a 31% drop on GAIA without the ledger orchestrator, and that agents rediscover sub-task solutions after resets.
- **Thresholds in practice:**

  | Signal | System | Threshold |
  |---|---|---|
  | Same action + same observation | OpenHands | 4 |
  | Same action + error | OpenHands | 3 |
  | Monologue | OpenHands | 3 messages |
  | A,B alternation | OpenHands | 6 steps |
  | Cycle of period 1–5 | Gemini CLI | 5 repeats |
  | Repeated text chunk | Gemini CLI | 10 times |
  | LLM loop judge | Gemini CLI | after 30 turns, confidence 0.9 |
  | Similar action in window of 20 | Browser Use | 5 / 8 / 12 |
  | Unchanged page fingerprint | Browser Use | 5 steps |
  | Consecutive failures | Browser Use | 3 replan nudge, 5 forced finish |
  | Step budget | Browser Use | warning at 75% |
  | Same action + same response | Reflexion | more than 3 cycles, or 30 actions |

- **Why small models repeat.** Repetition is self-reinforcing (Xu et al. 2022; Manus on agents imitating their own context). TIDE (2026) measures loop ratios of 36.7% for Qwen3-4B-Instruct against 5.7% for Qwen3-30B on WebShop, with low action entropy on loop steps. Thinking mode gave mixed results, and LLM-summarised memory lowered small-model scores.
- **Soft hints fail often.** In MIRAGE-Bench, with 3 or 6 repeats already visible in the history, models repeat unaware in 23% to 59% of cases (35% for Qwen2.5-7B).
- **Structural fixes have the measured gains.**
  - AgentOccam: reducing the action space and disabling scroll took Gemini-1.5-Flash from 11.6 to 24.2; the planning prompt added only 1.6.
  - SWE-agent: keeping the last 5 observations instead of full history gave +3 points, and rejecting invalid edits gave another +3.
  - Agent-E: code-computed change observation after every action, but no ablation isolates it.

**My inference on the hackathon failures**
Replaying the last 2 turns verbatim, including the model's own thought, plus a tail of identical result lines, is close to a worst case for self-reinforcement. A static warning repeated every turn becomes part of the repeated pattern, which fits it being ignored.

**The proposed algorithm (section 6)**
One deterministic `StallGuard` per investigator:
- **Gate before each action:** refuses stale targets and tabu actions, and cuts the rest of the batch.
- **Change line after each action:** code-computed, states what changed or that nothing did.
- **Stall counter:** fed by nothing-new turns, cycles over state-qualified keys, repeated thoughts, 4 turns without a new page, and 15 turns without a gain.
- **Escalation:** block, then forced choice (navigation model proposes, code filters, Clef picks), then restart from a code-built brief that keeps the tabu list, then park the question after 2 restarts.
- **Prompt changes:** never replay thoughts, a deduplicated attempt ledger, a case-file change line, and a required open-question id that is validated each turn.

I ran the guard code against synthetic sequences, not the recorded runs. The four failure patterns restart within 3 to 14 turns, and legitimate paging with gains never stalls. The simulation exposed two false positives in my first draft (same Next button read as a cycle; back-to-list blocked after four items), both fixed in the saved version. All thresholds are untested on the real system; the notes recommend replaying the six recorded runs through the guard first.

**Least-evidenced parts**
- No source measures refusal plus forced choice against a nudge, or a separate decision model as the chooser.
- No source isolates the effect of removing the previous thought, a tabu list, or a page diff.
- There is no loop data for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next itself.
